Exact differentiation verifies the full-system reciprocal map; derivative convolution shows one infectious maximum strictly after the E+I maximum. The first-contact comparison orders Vκ and thus strictly orders the peak coordinate, proving unique λ=1 minimum. W′≤sup J′−κW/ρ on the rising side gives the SIR endpoint limit. Local assumptions, infinite-parameter quantifiers, and finite-data exceptions are explicit. Standalone symbolic identities and numerical samples replay successfully; finite checks are corroborative only.

value.rationale: For SEIR control planning, the number of infections after the observed infectious-prevalence peak is a natural epidemic burden distinct from the total-active-infection peak. Exact rate swapping and the globally strict minimum at matched incubation-exit/recovery rates give a nontrivial nonmonotone structural effect: finite latent phases strictly reduce post-infectious-peak overshoot compared to either reciprocal extreme, while the classical SIR worst-case bound is sharp only in singular limits. The theorem applies to all supercritical reproduction ratios, not an arbitrary one-off parameter choice.
